where: Section 1, 'Why not solve exactly?' and Quiz Q7 answer
problem: The text says quantum phase estimation 'reads an eigenvalue of H bit by bit and returns E₀'. QPE returns an eigenvalue of H drawn according to the overlap of the prepared input state with the eigenvectors; it returns the ground energy only if the input state has large overlap with the ground state and enough ancilla qubits are used. As written, a student concludes QPE always outputs E₀.
fix: 'Quantum phase estimation (see Unit 4) reads an eigenvalue of H into a register of ancilla qubits. Started from a state with large overlap on the ground state, it returns E₀ with high probability; started from a state with poor overlap it can return an excited energy. It needs long coherent circuits and fault tolerance.' In the Q7 answer, write the same caveat instead of 'QPEA gives the exact eigenvalue'.

problem: 'no measurement noise can push ⟨H⟩ below E₀' is true only for the exact expectation value. A finite-shot estimate of ⟨H⟩ can and does land below E₀, which is exactly what the shot noise in Worked example part (e) produces, so the two statements look contradictory.
fix: 'The exact expectation ⟨H⟩ can never fall below E₀. A finite-shot estimate is random and can land on either side of the true value, which is why many shots are needed.'

problem: 'gives the exact derivative of the sampled expectation value' is imprecise. With a finite number of shots the shifted combination is a noisy estimate; the exactness of the rule applies to the analytic expectation value (no finite-difference truncation error).
fix: 'It uses two runs at θ ± π/2 and gives the exact derivative of the analytic expectation value; only shot noise is left, not a finite-difference approximation error.'

problem: Grover search and amplitude amplification do not compute ground-state energies; they speed up searching an unstructured set of candidates. Mentioning them here as the 'exact' alternative to VQE can make a student think Grover solves the ground-state problem.
fix: Either drop this sentence, or say plainly that Grover speeds up search problems such as finding a marked solution and is not an alternative method for ground-state energy estimation.

problem: 'a few layers of RY on both qubits and a CNOT between them, so three or four angles' — each such layer contributes two RY angles, so the count is always even (2 per layer); 'three' cannot occur.
fix: 'a few layers of RY on both qubits and a CNOT between them, so four or six angles (two per layer).'

problem: The abbreviation 'QPEA' is used without being introduced; the chapter calls the method 'quantum phase estimation (QPE)' and gives no '(see Unit 4)' pointer in the quiz answer.
fix: Use 'quantum phase estimation (QPE)' consistently, or write 'QPE algorithm (QPEA)' the first time.
